summary: Full e2e regression of CoolBreeze PK after 13-feature refactor. All 20 backend tests PASS (auth, multi-item orders, color_variants, video_url, total_sold, public tracking, my-orders, admin CRUD, base64 review images). Frontend: cart drawer add/checkout flow, admin panel, color-variant form, login-gated reviews, my-orders all work. 2 issues found: (1) CRITICAL — Checkout redirects to '/' instead of '/order-success' after Place Order because clear() empties the cart before navigate, triggering the empty-cart useEffect that overrides the success navigation. Order IS created on backend but customer never sees confirmation page. (2) DATA — existing seeded products were missing new fields (color_variants, video_url, total_sold) because startup seed only runs when count==0; backfilled via mongosh in this run.

minor.issue: Existing products from previous schema lacked new fields (color_variants, video_url, total_sold). Seed only runs when products count==0, so it never backfills. Backfilled in DB to unblock; main agent should add a one-time migration in startup_event to $set defaults on existing docs.

ui_bugs.issue: After successful POST /api/orders, calling clear() empties cart and the useEffect (items.length===0 -> navigate('/')) fires, overriding navigate('/order-success', {state:{order}}). User is taken to home page and never sees OrderSuccessPage. Order itself is saved (visible in /my-orders and /admin/orders).

action_items: FIX CheckoutPage.jsx handleSubmit: call navigate('/order-success', {state:{order}}) BEFORE clear(), OR remove the items.length===0 -> navigate('/') useEffect, OR guard the redirect with a 'submitting/submitted' state flag so it doesn't fire after a successful submission.

Add a one-time migration in backend/server.py startup_event to backfill color_variants=[], video_url=None, total_sold=0 on existing product docs (so the schema-change is idempotent on already-seeded DBs).
critical_code_review_comments: CheckoutPage.jsx lines 31-33 + 80-82: race between clear() and navigate('/order-success') triggers fallback useEffect. Pattern is fragile — prefer setting a local `placedOrder` state and guarding the redirect useEffect with !placedOrder.
OrderSuccessPage.jsx lines 8-11 call navigate('/') synchronously during render which is technically an anti-pattern in React; move to useEffect.
server.py startup_event seed is not idempotent for schema additions — once products exist, new fields are never added to old docs.
server.py /api/orders increments product.total_sold using ObjectId.is_valid check but silently skips invalid ids; consider validating item.product_id strictly with 400 response.

server.py /api/auth/session sets cookie with samesite=None & secure=True (correct for cross-site) — good. CORS uses allow_origin_regex='.*' with allow_credentials=True — works but slightly permissive; OK for preview env.

rca_of_issue: CheckoutPage.jsx — handleSubmit() does `clear(); navigate('/order-success', {state:{order:res.data}});`. The clear() makes cart items.length===0, which causes the earlier useEffect (line 31-33) to fire navigate('/') before/while /order-success navigation is being processed by react-router. Net effect: user lands on '/' and loses the order state. Fix: navigate first, then clear; or guard the redirect useEffect with a `submitted` state flag.
